title: On Releasing Annotator-Level Labels and Information in Datasets
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure any aspect of faith or religion. It analyzes how label aggregation in subjective annotation tasks (hate speech, sentiment, emotion) can under-represent the perspectives of certain socio-demographic groups.
findings: The paper does not present any findings related to religion, as it was not a focus of the study. The key findings are that aggregating annotator labels via majority vote can under-represent or ignore the perspectives of a substantial number of annotators. Furthermore, this effect is not uniform across socio-demographic groups; for instance, White annotators had significantly higher agreement with the majority label on a sentiment task than Black annotators, suggesting the final aggregated dataset better reflects the perspectives of the former group.
